sections.overview: This little-known libellulid dragonfly is the only described species in its genus.
sections.identification: The original description gives a body length of about 31 mm and hindwings around 25 mm; identification relies on details of wing venation and colour.
sections.habitat: It was first found beside a small sandy-bottomed stream in Suriname gallery forest; recent French Guianan records include savannas, open wetlands and drainage ditches.
sections.diet: The publications consulted provide no species-specific prey study, so its diet is not described more precisely here.
sections.behavior: In Suriname it was observed mainly high in trees, but adults sometimes descended to streamside vegetation and retreated upward when disturbed.
sections.reproduction: A recent French Guianan paper documents local observations and an emergence, but the species’ broader breeding biology remains poorly known.
sections.ecology: Known records come from few localities, and French Guianan observations broaden the habitats documented since the original forest records.
sections.conservation: Scattered records are insufficient to infer a population trend; recent observations show it also occurs beyond the originally reported canopy setting.
